tested: Cisco ASA (legacy; ASAv is in the main list as cisco-asav)

reasons.emulator:
qemu_version_default: EVE-NG's asa.yml pins `qemu_version: 4.1.0` - a
distinct pin from asav (2.12.0, see cisco-asav/asav above); this is the
older i386 physical-ASA-image platform, not ASAv.
qemu_arch x86_64 -> i386 (NPX-303/NPX-460, 2026-09-11): NPX-460's EVE-NG
template re-audit found exactly one real qemu_arch disagreement across all 171
matched templates - this one (EVE-NG's real asa.yml pins i386; netplex shipped
x86_64). Per netplex rule #33 (device_profiles.py must match the real EVE-NG
template, not be guessed), i386 is the correct permanent default regardless of
any one image's own boot outcome. LIVE-TESTED, honestly reported: the one real
classic-ASA image reachable anywhere (asa 8.0.2, imported from <vendor-box>) hit
an IDENTICAL kernel panic under BOTH x86_64 and this i386 setting, so the arch
change alone did not unblock it. SUPERSEDED 2026-09-22 (NPX-153): that panic was
never an arch problem and was NOT an external blocker - it was the RAM ceiling,
root-caused and fixed below (see the min/default/max_ram_mb comment). i386 stays
because it is the verified-correct EVE-NG-parity value;
a per-node qemu_arch override (backend/node-manager/providers/qemu.py) now also
exists if a future, non-broken classic-ASA image needs x86_64 instead.
nic: e1000 -> i82559er (NPX-303/NPX-1113, found 2026-09-14 live-testing the
asa 9.1.5 image): EVE-NG's real asa.yml (re-checked directly) pins
`qemu_nic: i82559er`, not e1000 - this was the one field NPX-460's earlier
template audit didn't catch (it only flagged the qemu_arch mismatch, fixed
separately below). Live evidence: booting this profile's e1000 NIC, the
ASA's own boot log shows "Driver not found for vid=0x8086 did=0x100e"
(0x100e is the e1000 PCI id) repeated for every configured interface, then
"Total NICs found: 0" and a kernel segfault soon after - the classic-ASA
firmware's own NIC driver simply doesn't recognize the e1000 model QEMU
was emulating. i82559er (an Intel 8255x Fast Ethernet chip) is what EVE-NG
verified works.
reasons.min_ram_mb:
rule #59 reason: ram 384 MB vs EVE-NG 2048 (initrd window, NPX-153) - RAM CEILING: THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE CLASSIC-ASA BOOT PANIC (NPX-153,
root-caused 2026-09-22). This is a deliberate, evidence-backed deviation from
EVE-NG's asa.yml (`ram: 2048`) - rule #59 requires the reason in writing, here it
is, with the guest kernel's own words.
The asa-8.02 disk boots via GRUB 0.91 on its MBR (stage1 -> /boot/grub/stage2 on
hda2). Its menu.lst says:
kernel /boot/vmlinuz root=/dev/hda1 ... initrd /boot/asa-single.gz
hda1 is a VFAT partition (the ASA flash: lina_monitor, ln) and this kernel
(2.6.17.8, 32-bit) has only ext3 + cramfs compiled in. The REAL root filesystem is
the initrd (`asa-single.gz`, a cpio initramfs containing /init), so `root=` is
never supposed to be reached at all.
GRUB legacy always parks the initrd near the TOP of RAM, capped at its own
LINUX_INITRD_MAX_ADDRESS (0x38000000 = 896 MB). This ASA kernel's low-memory
window ends at 0x1a000000 (it reports "416MB LOWMEM available" for any RAM size
>= 512 MB). So on any node with >= 512 MB the kernel prints, verbatim:
initrd extends beyond end of memory (0x1ffcf8af > 0x1a000000)
disabling initrd
...then falls through to the VFAT hda1 it cannot mount:
No filesystem could mount root, tried:  ext3 cramfs
Kernel panic - not syncing: VFS: Unable to mount root fs on unknown-block(3,1)
Measured boundary (asa 8.0.2, qemu-system-i386, EVE-NG's own option set AND
netplex's KVM path - both behave identically, so this is the image, not the
hypervisor flags): 256 MB and 384 MB load the initrd ("Freeing initrd memory:
1682k freed") and reach the real `ciscoasa>` prompt with "Total NICs found: 6";
512 MB, 1024 MB and 2048 MB all hit the panic above. 416 MB is the true hard
ceiling, but the UI RAM stepper moves in 128 MB steps, so 384 is the highest
selectable safe value and is pinned as max_ram_mb - raising it past this does not
give the firewall more memory, it stops the box booting at all.
This is why the "i386 vs x86_64" and NIC-model fixes before it never helped: the
panic happens before any of that matters. Nothing about -icount, -smbios
type=1,product=asa5520 or accel=tcg (all of which EVE-NG's asa.yml sets) is
required - each was tested directly and the image boots to `ciscoasa>` without
them under plain KVM, so netplex deliberately does NOT carry that drift.
